#2892. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

(See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.)

Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:

This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

From here, it's all about the follow through.  We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

Zscaler shares surged 18% in extended trading on Friday after Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy the cybersecurity vendor. Shares of CrowdStrike shares fell more than 8%.

CrowdStrike has been one of the big cybersecurity winners in the artificial intelligence boom, with its stock about doubling in value this year, lifting its market cap to $235 billion. Zscaler, meanwhile, is down 13% this year, pushing its market cap down to about $32 billion.

#2888. Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens 'tremendous tax'

President Donald Trump on Friday said U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so.

"We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.

"I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump said. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here."

Trump's latest push for more data-center construction in the U.S. came despite Americans repeatedly stating — and showing with their votes — that they dislike the structures.

CNBC's All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% of respondents said they would support one.

If Trump follows through on his threat to clamp down on overseas data center construction, he will have to contend with the fact that numerous U.S. tech giants — including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — have already built them in other countries.

International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements.

Trump said Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them."

"We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They're tremendous assets," Trump said.

Representatives at cloud providers Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's remarks came a day after Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for a trilateral summit that appeared to produce few concrete deliverables on an array of pressing global issues.

Xi "congratulated me on how well we're doing" in artificial intelligence, Trump said, using his preferred term "super intelligence," which he said the Chinese president also likes better.

— CNBC's Jordan Novet and Annie Palmer contributed reporting.

#2887. ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround

'It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers created their two cleanest late-game looks several hours before they needed them.

During Wednesday morning's shootaround in Orlando, Nick Nurse had the Sixers work on offensive material they had not consistently used this season. They tested one of those actions during the first half, returned to it throughout the closing minutes and watched it produce the shots they needed to complete a 17-point comeback.

"We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn't used before, and they ran all that stuff very, very well and very calmly and with composure," Nurse told reporters.

The Sixers have earned six of their 13 wins after trailing by double digits. They are also 11-0 in games that reached clutch time.

Relying on comebacks is not a sustainable plan. The repeated late-game situations, however, have forced a new roster to respond to different lineups, coverages and responsibilities while the season is still young.

Each close finish gives Nurse more information about which players and actions hold up when possessions tighten. Wednesday gave him a new option.

Anfernee Simons' clinching three in the Sixers' 121-116 win over the Magic was the final result of that preparation.

"That last play, we ran that play in the first half," Simons said. "We worked it a couple of times, and in the second half we ran that play every single time down the stretch, and it worked every time.

"It was a play we ran through. [It's gratifying] especially when it's working consistently and you're getting different shots out of it and the opposing team just don't know what to do.

"We just continue to run the play and get the open shots we need."

NBC Sports Philadelphia video producer and Sixers Talk podcast co-host Kevin Rice broke down how the Sixers used its different options to keep Orlando guessing.

The action begins with two players stationed near the elbows. A player on the opposite elbow then sets a screen for the player up top, who receives the ball while moving around it.

The Sixers ran the set three consecutive times during the first half. None of the possessions reached the primary option. Each still produced a quality opportunity.

On the first, Joel Embiid cleared LeBron James out of the area and directed Simons around him for a dribble handoff. Simons received an open three-point look.

Orlando took away the handoff the next time down but left Embiid one-on-one against Wendell Carter Jr. Embiid created enough room to retrieve his own miss and convert an and-one opportunity.

The third attempt pulled Orlando's defense into the paint. Two passes moved the ball through the collapsing coverage and created an open three for VJ Edgecombe.

"We had a little thing where he comes flying off behind Joel, and he doesn't get to do that that much, right?" Nurse said of Simons. "So tonight he gets the opportunity to do it, and it was very good for us on a number of plays."

The Sixers changed the action late without abandoning its initial Horns alignment. Simons moved through the lane to help form a Spain pick-and-roll involving James and Embiid.

On the first late possession, Simons remained near the play after James gained a matchup against Carter. Orlando struggled to sort out its assignments, leaving James open for a 19-foot jumper with 54.8 seconds remaining.

After Jalen Suggs made one of two free throws, the Sixers returned to the same setup. This time, Simons relocated to the left corner after James drew Carter on a switch.

James drove into the paint. Suggs lost track of Simons while responding to the penetration, and James sent the ball toward the corner.

Simons buried the open three to give the Sixers a 119-113 lead with 15 seconds left.

"Bron just penetrated the paint," Simons said. "It kind of got some confusion, and when I was on the dunker and kind of spaced out to the corner, I ended up finding myself wide open for the three, and Bron found me."

The Sixers entered the night without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, their two leading scorers. Simons made his first start with Philadelphia and recorded 18 points in the city where he grew up.

His final basket also illustrated why Nurse believes the Sixers have more to uncover with him.

"When he's out there, they gotta be really careful," Nurse said. "So I think there's some drives he creates, and just about every time he lets it go, whether he's on balance or not, you think it's going in, and that is a big deal. Like, that is a big deal.

"And again, I think we're still a ways away from really unlocking him to being even more part of some of the things we can do with him to create more shots."

Philadelphia is now 11-0 in clutch games. The finish in Orlando provided a more specific explanation than experience or shot-making alone.

The Sixers installed a set in the morning, explored its counters and trusted it when the game tightened. James supplied the patience to read Orlando's coverage. Embiid occupied the middle of the action. Simons moved without the ball, and Edgecombe remained ready to shoot.

James said his heart rate drops when close games increase the pressure on everyone else.

"I mean, experience," James said. "A guy that's seen every situation this league has to offer. It's nothing I haven't seen. And, you know, in the moments where people's heart rate goes up or anxiety goes up, mine is pretty low. It's actually lower, you know."

The Sixers still have more actions and reads to learn as Nurse becomes familiar with his new personnel, but their latest win showed their innate ability to adapt in big moments.

"I think we're still a long ways away from knowing all the reads and all that stuff because it's just a little early, right?" Nurse said.

So much for buying the dip.As the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq-100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 19% from highs as of midday Friday, the single biggest options trade of the day was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has a long way more to fall.Around 12:30 E.T., someone spent $93 million buying 20,000 380-strike puts expiring Sep. 17, 2027, according to trading data reviewed by SpotGamma and Volland, options-analytics platforms that both show the trade as a likely opening position, with volume exceeding existing open interest in the contract. The trade bets that the index will fall below $380, a nearly 8% decline from its current level. The SMH is off 40% from its recent all-time highs.

"That trade stands out big-time," wrote Jason DeLorenzo, founder and owner of Volland. "It is either a hedge or speculative, but either way it isn't a vote of confidence."The puts were bought for $46.50 a piece, an arguably expensive choice for a downside bet with volatility in the ETF trading at 70.

"You're paying a metric ton of Vega for that thing," added SpotGamma's Brent Kochuba, referring to the contract's sensitivity to changes in volatility of the underlying chip ETF. "Maybe they were a forced buyer, or maybe they're actually selling this, which can still be the case even though the price shows it happening closer to the ask."

The semiconductor index headed for a 9% drop this week alone.

#2883. How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch

How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

As he overtook Jason Kidd for the third-most assists in NBA history, LeBron James piloted the Sixers' offense down the stretch against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday.

With Joel Embiid sitting out and Tyrese Maxey getting a breather on the bench, James took over in the fourth quarter. He did so by spamming the same action over and over again.

The set consisted of James getting a ball screen from a guard – either VJ Edgecombe or Anfernee Simons – at the top of the key. After setting or ghosting the screen, the guard would short roll towards the basket.

When the Pacers blitzed or hedged the screen, James found the guard. The Sixers could then attack a 4-on-3 or 3-on-2 situation.

Twice, Edgecombe and Simons scored off the roll.

When the Pacers helped to the roller, that opened up the shooters in each corner.

James directed traffic on offense to ensure that the Sixers spaced the floor properly. Here, he waved Dean Wade out of the dunker spot and into the corner. Edgecombe promptly hit him for an open three off the short roll.

After all of the Sixers' success, the Pacers eventually switched the ball screen. That left the 6-foot-4, 173-pound Quenton Jackson on James, who has five inches and 77 pounds on him.

Jackson and James had already gone head to head on Sunday.

In the first quarter, James set a ball screen for Edgecombe which the Pacers switched. Edgecombe fed James in the post and the Pacers doubled him to support Jackson. James punished them for it.

They didn't double James after the switch in the fourth quarter. This time, James backed Jackson down, backed him down again and backed him down some more before scoring inside.

James' strength abusing matchups against smaller defenders after switches has been a safety valve for the Sixers' offense. Guards struggle to stop him from getting to the basket. When defenses send help, he picks them apart with his otherworldly passing ability.

That combination forced the Pacers to pick their poison. From the 9:55 mark in the fourth until the Pacers switched to a zone defense (after James bullied Jackson) with just over 6:00 left, the Sixers scored 13 points out of this action across seven possessions. That's a stellar 1.86 points per possession.

James, who's scoring a career-low 15.1 points per game so far this season, might not be the elite bucket-getter he was for most of his career. But he's still brilliant at conducting highly efficient offense that pressures a defense's pain points.

#2882. Warriors’ Steve Kerr Delivers Blunt Assessment Amid Injury-Hit Skid

It's been a rollercoaster start to the season for the Golden State Warriors. They began the campaign with three straight losses before turning things around and rattling off an eight-game win streak. Now, though, Steve Kerr's team finds itself on a five-game skid and without Stephen Curry, who is absent from the rotation due to a right oblique abdominal tear.

When speaking to the media on Thursday, November 19, ahead of the Warriors matchup with the Memphis Grizzlies, which Golden State ultimately lost 126-98, Steve Kerr provided a blunt assessment of the issues his team is currently facing.

"This is just where we are right now. We're wiped out with injuries," Kerr said, via Dalton Johnson. "The guys are really competing and playing hard and staying together and that's all we can do. Things are going to turn, but we've got to give ourselves the best chance."

Right now, the Warriors need patience. At some point this season, Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Curry will all return to the rotation. Once that happens, Golden State's rotation will look far stronger. Until then, the Warriors are going to endure some difficult stretches of basketball.

Fortunately for the Warriors, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked fantastic to begin his NBA career, and with so many high-usage players sidelined, he's being given the room and the green light to figure things out on the fly. The results might not be what fans are expecting, but the experience Lendeborg is currently gaining will be invaluable to his development.

Of course, Warriors fans won't want to hear that until the franchise has halted its latest skid down the Western Conference standings.

#2881. Nvidia stock plunges 14%, wraps up longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis

The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

Nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang. The stock closed lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

Shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion. The stock is now trading at roughly 8.4 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting issues at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

Once the most valuable company in the world, Nvidia now has a market cap of $3 trillion, putting it fourth behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet.

Nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms."

But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

Even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and said that customers aren't going anywhere.

On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this." In a company meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

For investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire company now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

#2879. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.  Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats! originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

This 76ers team is a heck of a lot of fun to watch and fun basketball means fun stats!

At 13-3, the 76ers are exactly a month into the 5th-best start in franchise history and best since they were 14-2 in 2000-01. Which turned out to be a pretty good year. They were 15-1 in 1949-50 and 1966-67 and 14-2 in 1981-82.

To help everybody get through this interminable two-day gap between 76ers games, here's our first 2026-27 installment of Roob's 76ers Stats, with a tip of the hat to Stathead.

→ The 76ers have been out-rebounded by 34 through 16 games (719-685) and their 13-3 record matches the best in NBA history by a team that's been out-rebounded after 16 games. Three other teams have been 13-3 despite getting out-rebounded, most recently the 2013-14 Miami Heat. The others are the 1979-80 Bucks and 2012-2013 Spurs. The 76ers are an NBA-best 6-3 this year when they've been out-rebounded (which means they're 7-0 when they have a rebounding edge).

→ In the win over Orlando Thursday, V.J. Edgecombe had 24 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, and Joel Embiid had 26 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. It was the first time two 76ers had at least 24 points, six rebounds and assists and two steals in a game in 53 years. In a win over the Celtics at the Spectrum in 1973, Fred Carter had 31 points, six rebounds, six assists and seven steals and George McGinniss had 28 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists and three steals.

→ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a career 37 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 44 percent so far. Anfernee Simons, a career 38 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 41 percent. Jabari Walker, a career 33 percent 3-point shooter, is at 42 percent. Dean Wade, a career 37 percent shooter, is at 41 percent. Jaylen Brown, a career 36 percent shooter from range, is at 39 percent. The 76ers are shooting just 36 percent as a team from the stripe because James and Embiid have been so bad, but everybody else is off to career-best starts from 3-point range.

→ The 76ers are 7-1 on the road, equalling their best road record ever after eight games. They were also 7-1 in 1980-81, 1981-82 and 1982-83. The 1981 team had the best road start in franchise history, going 12-1 before losing its second road game.

→ With 15.7 points, 6.8 assists and 6.8 rebounds per game, LeBron James is only the fifth 76er ever to average at least 15 ½ points and 6 ½ assists and rebounds through 16 games. The others are some familiar names: Wilt Chamberlain in 1967, Charles Barkley in 1987, Ben Simmons in 2018 and James Harden in 2023.

→ The 76ers already have more wins this year after trailing by 10 points through the first quarter than all but two full seasons since 1950. They had four in 1985-86 and again in 2022-23. The Hawks also have three wins this year when trailing by double digits after the first quarter, but they're 3-4 and the 76ers are 3-2. So they actually have a winning record when they're down by double digits going into the second quarter.

→ With Jaylen Brown (22.6, 6.6), Joel Embiid (20.0, 8.3), LeBron James (15.7, 6.8) and V.J. Edgecombe (13.6, 6.5), the 76ers are the only NBA team with four players averaging 6 ½ rebounds and 13 points. The last time they had four players in a season who averaged 13 points and 6 ½ rebounds was 1961-62 when they were the Syracuse Nationals, with Dave Gambee (16.7, 7.9), Hal Greer (22.8, 7.4), Red Kerr (16.3, 14.7), Dolph Schayes (14.7, 7.8) and Lee Shaffer (16.9, 6.8).

→ Edgecombe's 6.5 rebounds per game are 2nd-most among shooting guards behind only the Grizzlies' Cedric Coward, who is at 8.5. Edgecombe's 6.5 is also 2nd-highest ever by a 76ers shooting guard behind only Greer's 7.4 during that 1961-62 season. Edgecombe averaged 5.6 rebounds as a rookie and his 5.8 career average is highest by a shooting guard who spent more than one year with the 76ers. Greer is second at 5.3. Among all NBA players who've played at least 90 games, Edgecombe's 5.8 average is 11th-highest all-time among shooting guards (although Stathead includes some swing guard-forwards in their data).

→ Joel Embiid's 14.6 shooting percentage from 3 is worst in NBA history after 16 games (minimum 40 attempts). Embiid is 6-for-41 from the stripe this year. The previous 3-point shooting low 16 games into a season belonged to Cedric Ceballos of the Lakers in 1995-96 and the 76ers' Evan Turner in 2013-14. Both were 6-for-43 for 16.3 percent.

→ LeBron James is at 22.2 percent from 3 on 10-for-45. The Sixers are the first NBA team in 12 years with two players under 23 percent after 16 games with a minimum of 40 attempts. In 2014 Tony Wroten was 10-for-50 (10 percent) and Turner was 6-for-43 (16.3 percent).

#2877. Carson Beck dealing with back spasms, Josh Johnson in line to start vs. Chiefs

The Cardinals may have a fourth starting quarterback in four weeks when they play the Chiefs on Sunday.

Rookie Carson Beck is once again dealing with back spasms, which puts veteran backup Josh Johnson in line to start in Week 11.

Beck made his regular-season debut last week in the 34-6 loss to the Rams. He was able to practice in full on Wednesday but was listed as limited for Thursday’s session.

The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season.

“It’s basically just responding to the treatment, see how he feels when he wakes up tomorrow,” head coach Mike LaFleur said in his Friday press conference.

LaFleur added that he doesn’t think Beck will be out multiple weeks with the injury, but he’s unsure at this point.

“You go with the people who know what they’re doing to treat it. It’s not like this is the first time he’s dealt with it,” LaFleur said. “We’ll see more tomorrow.”

If Johnson does start, it will be his first time playing for Arizona in the regular season and add to his long list of clubs. Johnson has appeared in regular-season games for seven teams, including the Jets back in 2021 when LaFleur was the team’s offensive coordinator.

“Cool part is, if it is Josh, I’ve called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him,” LaFleur said. “So, we’ll go shoot our shot and I expect nothing less from our guys.”

Still, the instability within Arizona’s QBs room is remarkable. In Week 8, Jacoby Brissett made his last start for the club before Gardner Minshew came in and engineered a comeback to send the game to overtime, ultimately beating the Cowboys. Minshew then started Week 9 against Seattle, but suffered a season-ending elbow injury in the loss. Beck made his first start last Sunday and now Johnson is in line to be under center against Kansas City.

The Cardinals’ full injury report with game statuses will be released later on Friday.

#2876. AFC North Week 10 Recap: Browns pull off another comeback

Three teams in the AFC North appear poised for a playoff push down the final stretch of the season.

The Bengals took the division lead with a 38-18 dismantling of the Steelers on Sunday Night Football.

No quarterback has played better than Joe Burrow over the past month. Against Pittsburgh, he completed 35 of 44 pass attempts for 406 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow is now the betting favorite to win MVP with a league-high 27 passing touchdowns through 10 weeks. His top target, Ja'Marr Chase, has been red-hot as well in recent weeks, culminating in his best game of the season against the Steelers with 231 receiving yards on 11 catches. Chase Brown led the team in rushing with 44 yards on 10 carries while adding 39 yards and a pair of touchdowns on eight receptions. Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample accounted for Burrow's other two touchdowns.

Cincinnati's free agent additions continue to show up on defense as both Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen had sacks against Pittsburgh, bringing the pair's combined sack total to 10.5 on the season.

The Steelers fell to 6-3 and second place in the division with their 38-18 loss to the Bengals.

Pittsburgh found themselves in a 31-3 hole to start the fourth quarter. It was only then that Aaron Rodgers and the offense found some rhythm with consecutive touchdown drives. Rodgers finished the game with 15 completions on 29 attempts for 143 yards and a pair of touchdown passes — one to DK Metcalf, who led the team with 54 receiving yards on two catches, and the other to Pat Freiermuth. Jaylen Warren struggled to get going on the ground, rushing seven times for just 15 yards. Instead, it was fourth-year running back Lew Nichols who led the team with 43 rushing yards on six carries.

The Steelers' defense had no answers for Burrow and Cincinnati's passing attack. Patrick Queen had the defense's lone sack of the night while Payton Wilson racked up 19 total tackles.

After starting the game down 17-0, the Browns rallied to defeat the Houston Texans, 27-24, to improve to 6-4.

Deshaun Watson returned to the field after missing Week 9, completing 25 of 40 pass attempts for 312 yards and an interception while adding a team-high 49 yards and one touchdown on eight carries. This was Watson's sixth fourth-quarter comeback this season. Harold Fannin Jr. continues to look like a rising star at the tight end position as he led the team with 91 receiving yards on seven catches.

As usual, Carson Schwesinger led Cleveland's defense with 13 total tackles. Isaiah McGuire had the only sack on C.J. Stroud while Tyson Campbell came away with an interception in the second quarter.

The Ravens suffered their fifth straight loss in Week 10, falling 23-20 to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers.

Veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett made his debut at quarterback for Baltimore after just 10 days with the team. Brissett threw the ball 49 times, completing 33 passes for 340 yards and an interception. Mark Andrews seemed to have an immediate connection with his fourth quarterback of the season, leading the team with 82 receiving yards on eight catches — both season highs. While the passing attack found life for the first time in weeks, the run game was the complete opposite. Derrick Henry was repeatedly hit behind the line of scrimmage, finishing the game with just 10 yards on 10 carries, though he did find the end zone twice.

The Ravens' defense continues to be a disappointment under Jesse Minter. Omarion Hampton had his best game of the season, crossing 100 rushing yards for the first time in a game this year. This was also the first game that Justin Herbert did not throw an interception all season. Mike Green was a bright spot for the unit at least, with two sacks on Herbert and several strong plays against the run.

#2875. Colts release QB Daniel Jones

We predicted that Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will be benched, sooner than later. Technically, he has been.

The Colts have announced that Jones has been released.

It accelerates a process that would have begun with the Colts benching Jones to avoid having a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 becoming a full guarantee if Jones were to suffer a serious injury over the balance of the season. Jones would have then asked to be released, and the Colts would have likely done it.

So the Colts went straight to the final move on the chess board.

Jones will, once officially released, go to waivers. If/when (when) he clears waivers, he’ll become a free agent.

That’s the same thing that happened in 2024, after the Giants benched Jones and he asked to be released. He later signed with the Vikings, remaining there for the rest of the season before signing with the Colts in March 2025.

#2874. Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory

Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stretched their winning streak to four games and snagged a strong road win Wednesday night over the Magic.

They earned a 121-116 victory in Orlando to improve to 13-3 on the season. The Magic dropped to 6-8.

Joel Embiid had 26 points, seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks and two steals.

VJ Edgecombe posted a season-high 24 points, eight boards and six assists.

LeBron James scored 22 points and Anfernee Simons added 18.

Magic star Franz Wagner had 27 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds.

The Sixers had a long injury list in Orlando. Tyrese Maxey (right foot soreness), Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain) and Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness) were among their players out. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters in Orlando that Brown will be re-evaluated when the team returns to Philadelphia.

Orlando was without star forward Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain).

The Sixers will start a three-game homestand when they face the Bucks on Saturday afternoon. Here are observations on their win over the Magic:

The Sixers' undermanned starting lineup was Edgecombe, Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid.

After scoring 37 points in the Sixers' win over the Nets, Embiid had a subpar start. He began 1 for 6 from the floor and committed a turnover that led to an Anthony Black dunk.

The Sixers' lineup looked exactly like a unit that hadn't built any chemistry yet. The team was not sharp early on either end of the floor.

Desmond Bane drained a long three-pointer to give Orlando a 27-12 advantage. Orlando made 11 of its first 14 field goals and led by as many as 17 points in the first quarter.

Labaron Philon Jr. and Justin Edwards joined the Sixers' rotation. So did two-way contract players Tacko Fall and Caleb Love.

Philon impressed in the first quarter, converting two floaters and a corner three. The rookie passed his previous NBA scoring high of five points and finished the night with 10 on 4-for-5 shooting.

Fall played 10 minutes and posted two points, three rebounds and three blocks. He slammed in a dunk and rejected two shots early in the second quarter. Credit to Fall for giving the Sixers a good backup center performance and doing his job as a rim-protecting ultra-big man.

Love entered in the second quarter and was ready to fire, hitting a catch-and-shoot three-pointer on his first touch.

The Sixers' zone defense also helped them eat into the Magic's lead. The zone seemed to disrupt Orlando's offensive rhythm and it was active enough to prevent the Magic from consistently creating high-quality looks.

Edgecombe's buzzer-beating mid-range jumper cut the Sixers' deficit to 69-64 after two quarters.

The Sixers pulled within a single point on multiple occasions in the third quarter, including on a Philon three late in the period. They trailed by five points after the third.

Fall continued to play well early in the fourth quarter. He deterred the Magic's drivers from getting all the way to the rim as the very large back line of the Sixers' zone defense and made eye-catching hustle plays on both sides of the ball.

The Sixers outscored Orlando by seven points on the night with Fall on the court. Soon after Embiid subbed back in, he evened the game at 104-all with two free throws. Jabari Walker swished a three to finally push the Sixers in front.

The Magic regained a late lead with a Jalen Suggs three. James then drove and kicked the ball out to Edgecombe, who nailed one of his customary clutch jumpers to put the Sixers back on top.

No matter the night-to-night personnel, the Sixers have been fantastic at the tail end of close games. They're now 11-0 in clutch situations, which the NBA defines as games within a five-point differential in the final five minutes.

#2870. Average Four Factor Index Power Rankings: 2026-2027 NBA Season Week 5

After another week of play (which has amounted to 3-4 additional games for most teams), the young season is rounding into form, and the aFFI rankings are coming into sharper focus. In particular, the data are beginning to suggest the emergence of clear tiers of contention, though there are also a handful of teams that are moving rapidly up or down the list. Let's dig in to the numbers!

Regarding the Silver and Black, the last week has seen some exceptional performances (e.g., against Golden State) balance against statistically unremarkable wins and one clunky loss to Detroit. Figure 1 (below) shows that this combination has resulted in the Spurs staying put in fourth place, though the margin separating the top five positions is razor thin (more on that later). San Antonio's overall aFFI value continues to be weighed down by an ∆EFG% value (54.72) that – while above average – is well below almost any other team that is considered a legitimate contender. Even so, the Spurs are doing quite well with respect to the other three differentials, with particularly excellent average percentiles in ∆ORB% (65.81) and ∆FTM/FGA (66). In summary, the Spurs excellent start to the season has leaned heavily on their ability to protect the ball, rebound, and get to the free throw line relative to their opponents.

Stepping back to review the league as a whole, one striking finding in Figure 1 is that there are a number of teams that have risen or fallen rapidly in the last week. Here are some exceptional standouts:

Memphis Grizzlies (↑8) – After Memphis started the season 6-0, they went on a three-game losing streak and seemed destined to be a promising young team that was ultimately unready to become a true contender. However, they have been on an absolute tear recently, riding exceptional effective field goal differentials (their average ∆EFG% percentile of 70.87 is by far the best in the league) to the top of the aFFI rankings. The Grizzlies continue to have some serious flaws (e.g., a dreadful average ∆TOV% percentile), but they are undoubtedly a team to watch.

Miami Heat (↑5) – Miami's 0-4 start was cringeworthy, and they have a long way to go to join this season's truly elite teams. Having said that, their current six-game win streak has included some impressive wins, and their aFFI value has risen above league average due to some excellent average ∆TOV% (60.24) and ∆FTM/FGA (61.58) percentiles.

Golden State Warriors (↓9) – The young season has already been quite a roller coaster ride for the Warriors. They started slow, but went on a hot streak driven in part by some exceptional performances by rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Unfortunately, that magic has not continued with Steph Curry out of the lineup, and Golden State is currently on a five-game skid that includes four blowout losses.

Brooklyn Nets (↓8) – Let me be clear here: The Nets' aFFI value was never good; however, one week ago it would have been fair to say that Brooklyn was playing like a team that should win about 40% of it's games, even though they were actually winning about half as often. The games played since then suggest that this lukewarm initial assessment was likely a statistical quirk.

Looking at Figure 2 (below), we can see that teams are beginning to separate into distinct aFFI groupings, which provides us the opportunity to classify teams into tiers. At present, I see four tiers, though as time goes on teams that number is likely to rise:

Early Contenders (8 teams) – At present, there are eight teams that have an aFFI value of 56.28 or more, with the 9th-ranked Knicks (53.61) trailing the early contenders by a healthy margin of over 2.5 points. The first month of play suggests that any of these teams could emerge as true championship contenders as the season goes on, though if we're being honest this group could probably be subdivided further. In particular, the top five teams (Memphis, Minneapolis, Houston, San Antonio, and Boston) are noticeably ahead of everyone else and very close to each other, with the aFFI gap between the first-ranked Grizzlies and fifth-ranked Celtics (1.44 points) being just a bit larger than the gap between Boston and the sixth-ranked Lakers (1.21 points).

Likely Playoff/Play-in Participants (8 teams) – This is an interesting group for several reasons. First, it includes teams that are clearly heading in different directions. In particular, Dallas and Golden State appear to be at very high risk of falling to the tier below, whereas nearly every other member of this tier has seen their aFFI ranking rise in the last week. Philly remains by far the most interesting team in this set, as their stellar 13-3 record remains far out of step with a much more modest aFFI value (51.9). The 76ers' record will almost certainly move to 14-3 after they play the woeful Bucks tomorrow. However, after that they'll enter a difficult stretch of games that should reveal a lot about their true status.

Downslope to the Abyss (12 teams) – This is most crowded tier, with a correspondingly varied collection of outlooks. However, based on the first month of play, the best that most of these teams can hope for is a spot in the play-in (an opportunity that some of them will undoubtedly get, especially in the East). Within this group, the most interesting is clearly Atlanta, as its current record (9-6) is much more competitive that its 18th-ranked aFFI value (47.63) would suggest. Whether or not the Hawks can continue to beat the odds will be of particular interest to the Spurs, who are owed Atlanta's pick in the 2027 draft.

Kings' Corner (2 teams) – The Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks have collectively played 30 games, yet possess just two wins between them (one for each team). With their season over before the end of November, Bucks fans are already turning toward implausible draft and trade scenarios that will rescue them from obscurity. In stark contrast, Kings fans forgot long ago that any other state of being was possible.

Data Source: The underlying data used for this analysis was collected from Basketball Reference.

#2868. Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

(This is the Warren Buffett Watch newsletter, news and analysis on all things Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway. You can sign up here to receive it every Friday evening in your inbox.)

Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

The much more widely held B shares closed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the company's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance."

The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

Two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds."

#2866. Mets' initial offer to Tarik Skubal was reportedly for 9 years, nearly $400 million

The New York Mets are considered the frontrunner for two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. They have a track record of spending big, and there's reason to think they'll pony up to secure the left-handed hurler, who is the most prized free agent this offseason.

Their initial offer to the 30-year-old southpaw reportedly already gave him the opportunity to make contract history.

Former Mets general manager and current MLB Network Radio analyst Jim Duquette reported on Friday that the offer in question was for nine years and nearly $400 million. That yearly mark of $44.4 million would result in the highest average annual value (AAV) for a free agent starting pitcher ever.

At the moment, the current AAV record in that department is held by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander, both of whom the Mets previously inked to deals worth $43.3 million in AAV.

In November 2021, New York signed Scherzer to a three-year, $130 million contract. The following offseason, the Mets brought aboard Verlander on a two-year, $86.6 million deal. When those signings occurred, Scherzer and Verlander were in their late 30s. Granted they have six Cy Young Awards between them, but they were entering the final chapters of their illustrious careers.

Scherzer spent a season and a half with the Mets before being shipped off to the Texas Rangers during the 2023 season. Verlander was also moved ahead of the trade deadline that year, landing back with the Houston Astros.

If the Mets are able to reel in Skubal, though, they'll be getting him in his prime.

Skubal starred for the Detroit Tigers before the Los Angeles Dodgers acquired him leading up to this year's deadline. He joined an already stacked Dodgers roster that ultimately proved vulnerable down the stretch. The Milwaukee Brewers denied L.A. a championship three-peat, sweeping the Dodgers in the NLCS en route to winning the World Series.

Now Skubal has to decide if he wants to stay in L.A. or go elsewhere for the 2027 season and beyond.

The Dodgers are reportedly vying for his long-term services, as are the Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres, as well as the Mets, of course.

The Mets' initial offer was reportedly steep. Time will tell where and for how much Skubal eventually signs, and if he does so before the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1.

#2865. NBA trade rumors 2026-27: Dejounte Murray update (or, non-update), Kyrie Irving, Trey Murphy, more

Don't expect any NBA trades before Dec. 15, when many of the players who signed new contracts or extensions this summer become eligible to be traded. Even then, it's more likely we'll get closer to the February trade deadline before we see any notable names moved. That includes the guy in the sub-headline below.

While the insatiable NBA rumor mill keeps trying to find clickable updates on Dejounte Murray trades — "The Pelicans talked to the Suns!!!" — the reality is there is no traction toward any kind of deal for the New Orleans guard. Grant Liffman and Chris Mannix break it down well in the video above, but here is the latest.

• Murray, through his agents at Klutch Sports, made a trade request, and the Pelicans publicly acknowledged that, saying, "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization." New Orleans hasn't found that yet. Meanwhile, Murray's body language on the court betrays how unhappy he is, and he is shooting 29.6% from 3-point range this season, which doesn't help his trade value.

• To be blunt, teams around the league view Murray as a negative value contract. Those are hard to trade. The fact he is making $32.8 million this season and has a $30.8 million player option for next season also gives teams pause. He is viewed as a 30-year-old guard who's shot 41.9% overall and 30% from 3 in the last two-plus seasons.

• While Murray's camp seems to continue to push the Suns as a destination, league sources have told NBC Sports the Suns have minimal interest, unless the Pelicans want to attach sweetener, such as a first-round pick. That's been reported a lot of other places as well, it's no secret. While the Suns could use a point guard and have done background work on Murray (according to Brian Windhorst of ESPN), they aren't sold on Murray being the All-Star player he was five years ago, and he hasn't looked the same coming off his torn Achilles. How much interest the Pelicans have in Jalen Green should be another question.

• When teams do call the Pelicans, they are more likely to ask about Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones. But Joe Dumars is keeping the price ridiculously high — the Pelicans turned down a trade that would have netted them at least two first-round picks for Murphy over the summer, Michael Scotto of Hoopshype reports.

• Jake Fischer of The Stein Line reports the Suns are more interested in adding a big man with Mark Williams out for the season.

• Utah is one of the teams giving "internal consideration" a potential Kyrie Irving trade, if (or, more likely when) the Mavericks start listening to offers, reports Ian Begley of SNY.TV.

It's worth noting that teams have internal discussions about a lot of players and deals that they never even bother to reach out to the other team about in a serious manner, and where Irving fits in the young timeline in Utah is a good question, but the rumor is out there.

• Multiple reports have coach Brian Keefe's seat in Washington getting hot. This was a team that made moves for veterans in Anthony Davis (playing well) and Trae Young (not playing well) to try and win now, and with the team off to a 5-11 start, someone may be the scapegoat. Washington should have just pivoted to building around AJ Dybantsa, but they are going to be stuck with that horrible four-year, $212 million extension they gave Young this summer for a while. That is the most untradable contract in the league right now.

• Multiple reports have teams interested in trading for Bulls guard Tre Jones. Here is what Zach Lowe said on his Ringer podcast: "Teams are already calling the Bulls about Tre Jones... if he's not the best backup point guard in the NBA, he's very close. If they trade him, they're gonna get real stuff."

#2864. Colts' mismanagement continues with release of QB Daniel Jones

The Colts arguably mishandled the Jonathan Taylor situation, when it comes to the possibility of trading him. As to the possibility of trading Daniel Jones, there’s no argument to be made.

He has played two games since the deadline came and went, and now he’s been cut. They should have seen it coming.

Now? They get nothing. They’ll pay him $50 million for 11 games and have three wins to show for it.

The Vikings were interested, and they were talking to the Colts. While Minnesota wanted Kirk Cousins, the Colts could have lowered the price to a point that the Vikings couldn’t have refused.

Then again, the Vikings may have used the possibility of pivoting to Jones to get the Raiders down to a third-round pick for Cousins.

Regardless, the Colts blew it. It’s no surprise. They have no General Manager. Which makes it hard to generally manage the decisions that come with the opportunities to trade players.

Our guess is that the trades of guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner created the perception that the Colts were having a fire sale. Which resulted in lower offers for players like Taylor and Jones.

In the end, they traded neither. Now, Jones is gone. Taylor possibly will ask to be traded after the season, or they’ll decide to do it again on their own. Chances are that, when they do, they’ll get less than they could have gotten if they’d traded him at the deadline.

Will Anderson Jr. #51 of the Houston Texans sacks Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts for a safety in Houston, Texas, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Getty Images

Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones talks to the media following an NFL football game against the Houston Texans in Houston, Nov. 19, 2026. AP Photo/David J. Phillip

#2862. Nick Saban Makes Strong Statement on Alabama’s Controversial No. 3 Ranking

The Alabama Crimson Tide are 8-2 overall and coming off a 20-6 victory over the Vanderbilt Commodores last weekend.

Once again, the College Football Playoff committee continues to value Alabama quite highly, ranking the Crimson Tide No. 3 in its latest standings.

While many people may consider that a fair ranking, the criteria the committee uses to evaluate these teams simply don't make much sense.

For context, the Tennessee Volunteers are also 8-2, just like Alabama. Tennessee also beat the Crimson Tide 26-10 in their head-to-head matchup back in October. But where does Tennessee rank? No. 9, six spots behind Alabama.

Longtime Alabama coach and current "College GameDay" analyst Nick Saban appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Friday afternoon.

Saban discussed the Crimson Tide and made it clear that he has no influence over the committee's decisions about Alabama's ranking. In fact, he believes the Crimson Tide are not one of the three teams with the "right stuff" to win the national championship right now.

"I have nothing to do with the College Football Playoff, so I don't call anybody," Saban said. "So let's clear that air. I do think this is Kalen DeBoer's team. I do think they have a good team. It's hard to say who should be ranked where.

"Especially with the diversity of strength of schedule, trying to be sort of instituted in this in a not-so – I don't know how you would say it, but it's just very hard to do in college football, because there's a big deviation in quality of play, quality of teams, quality of players. I think it's very difficult for them not to be too subjective about how they try to go about ranking these teams."

The Crimson Tide have two regular-season games remaining against Chattanooga and Auburn.

But DeBoer isn't concerned with Alabama's position in the rankings. He made it clear that his team will focus on preparing for its next opponent and won't let the committee's decisions affect its approach.

"Tell us when we need to go, where to go, when to be there and who we're playing, and we'll be ready," DeBoer said earlier this week.

#2855. Shane Steichen: Daniel Jones didn't ask to be released

The Colts abruptly released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday. When coach Shane Steichen spoke to reporters on Friday, he was asked whether Jones asked to be cut.

“No, this was a decision that was just made for both, you know, the best interests of both parties,” Steichen said, via James Boyd of The Athletic.

Steichen also explained the timing by saying, “It’s just where we’re at in our season. . . . That’s just the situation that we’re at right now.”

The situation was clear. Jones was going to be benched, in order to ensure that he won’t suffer an injury that will trigger a $10.51 million guarantee for 2027. If that had happened, he would have been asked to be cut. And they likely would have done it.

So they accelerated it. Skipped steps. Got to where they would have landed after doing the dance.

Steichen also said that, as expected, Anthony Richardson will become the starter.

So instead of squatting on Jones and not letting him play, Jones gets a chance to land with a contender as a backup. Likely on the practice squad, which would give him the ability to jump to an active roster if/when a starter gets injured.

#2852. Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

I picked against the Vikings last week in Green Bay. I'm not doing that again. I lean towards San Francisco in this matchup, partially based on the fact that their quarterback has been on their team all season. It should be a great football game that will be decided by just a few plays.

This has all the makings of a game-of-the-year candidate. Brock Purdy has been great against pressure this year, but we'll see how he handles the pressure Flores' defense will bring this weekend. With aother week in the offense and some confidence off last week's win, I think Kirk Cousins looks and plays even better when the Vikings need a big performance.

I predicted the Vikings to lose to the Packers and was proven demonstrably wrong. I therefore have no choice but to keep my record going for the greater good and go for a 49ers win. #2848. Saints at Bears Q&A: Dennis Allen Revenge Game Part 2

The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the weak NFC South.

To help get you set for this matchup, we sat down with Nic Jennings of our sister site, Canal Street Chronicles (SB Nation's New Orleans Saints site), to get you set for their opponent.

1. The Saints are sitting at 3-6, but from my outsider view, I feel like this team is close to clicking, potentially even the back half of this season and start winning some football games. What's the vibe around the Saints for the fan base?

The vibe around the fanbase isn't great right now. I don't think fans have given up on the players, but rather they've given up on Kellen Moore, Mickey Loomis, and Gayle Benson. The Saints are somehow only one game out of first place in the division, so there's still hope that they can turn things around and make a push. But it is frustrating to watch a roster with this much talent continue to fail to put everything together. At this point, I think changes need to be made within the regime, and until that happens, I expect the vibes around the fanbase to remain largely the same, win or lose.

2. I'll be honest, when Kellen Moore was hired, I didn't think much of him as a head coaching candidate, but I've come around on him a little. What did Saints fans think of the hire last year, ar and where are they at with him midway through 2026?

The initial reaction to Moore's hiring was that the Saints finally had another offensive-minded head coach in the building who could bring a refreshing change to the way things had been done. However, that optimism has long since faded. Moore is running out of excuses, and quite frankly, I don't think there is any way he can win the fanbase back at this point. Through his first 26 games, the Saints have trailed in every single one of those games, while failing to score in the first quarter 18 times. Two consistent issues have plagued Moore's teams across both seasons: slow starts that force the Saints to claw their way back into games and an offense that continues to look dysfunctional, with a putrid run game forcing Tyler Shough to carry the team on his back. At this point, the frustration has gone beyond results, and fans are rightfully questioning whether Moore is the guy to lead this team moving forward.

3. I've never been a fan of how Mickey Loomis has handled the cap and the rebuild/reload (whatever you want to call it) of this roster. Are Saints fans still behind Loomis or do they want to see a change?

Yes, the fanbase still wants a change in the front office, but it's not necessarily because of the financial side of things. The Saints are expected to finally be out of "cap hell" next season and back to operating with more financial flexibility. However, Mickey Loomis' draft-day decisions and head coaching hires since Sean Payton's departure have taken their toll on the fanbase. For a team that has been in a rebuilding phase, it's difficult to get out of that cycle without consistently drafting impactful players, and that's been one of the biggest issues. The tricky part is that Loomis is the NFL's longest-tenured general manager at 25 years and has won a Super Bowl with the franchise. Given his history and relationship with the organization, I don't see Gayle Benson moving on from him unless he decides to step down himself. That's what makes the situation so complicated.

4. Tyler Shough certainly looks like he's taking strides this year, but he's also 27 years old. Do you think Shough is a legit NFL QB that can lead this Saints offense for the next 5 to 7 years?

Absolutely. Shough is the real deal, and his teammates rally behind him. He's been one of the few consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Carl Granderson.

Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He's carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket, and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven't really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He's shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most.

I do think there are still things he can improve on, and he's had a bit of a rough stretch over the last two weeks. Like I previously mentioned, the offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I'd put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. Though,gh to Shough's credit, the Saints have a nonexistent rushing attack, which hasn't eased the pressure on Shough and the passing game one bit.

But overall, I've seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans.

As for his age, to put things into perspective, Drew Brees joined the Saints at 27 years old, and it felt like he was in New Orleans for a lifetime. Even as a 26-year-old rookie, Shough was visibly more prepared than his fellow rookies. I view his age as a benefit rather than a drawback and believe he has a long career ahead of him.

5. What is one player on the Saints offense and one player on the Saints defense that may not be a headliner that you think can make an impact on Sunday? Do you have a prediction for the game?

After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas.

He's quickly become one of Tyler Shough's favorite targets and has established himself as the go-to guy in third-and-long situations.

With Jordyn Tyson back in the mix alongside Chris Olave, Vele's production has dwindled a bit over the past two games. That said, I believe his opportunities will come, and he's proven he can take advantage of them.

For a six-foot-five receiver to move the way he does and possess that type of body control is truly remarkable.

On defense, keep an eye on second-year defensive back, Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently "intended" to throw the football forward.

With Justin Reid now out of the picture in New Orleans, perhaps we see Sanker move back to his natural position at safety, where he spent his rookie season.

#2845. AMD dives on short seller report of alleged China exposure

Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem."

Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."

CNBC did not independently verify this information.

Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips."

The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

"The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson said in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity."

Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

#2842. Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers

Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.

The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent.

That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary.

Once he clears waivers, however, he'll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won't be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he's been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary.

Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings' practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

Michael Thorbjornsen won the Rocket Classic in July and has already locked up his playing privileges for next season on the PGA Tour, but he detailed what the players at the RSM Classic endured on a cold, windy day on St. Simons Island, Georgia, that was better suited for indoor activities.

"Some of the toughest stretch of golf I've ever had to pay," said Thorbjornsen, who played alongside Brooks Koepka and Blades Brown. "You'd pay money on every tee box for a par."

"On hole 1, I think Brooks, Blades and I hit our drives around 240 (yards) straight into the wind. That kind of shows what it was like out there," he said. "I don't think I've ever hit a drive that short in my life, condition-wise."

Well, the good news is there's only 36 holes to go in the RSM Classic and Thorbjornsen managed a 3-under 69, his 10th round of 69 or better at either the Seaside or Plantation courses at Sea Island Resort. That lifted him to 9-under 133 and a share of the lead at the midway point with Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen.

The bad news? It's probably going to be raining sideways with wind forecasted to gust up to 40 miles per hour on Saturday.

"It is what it is," Thorbjornsen said of the third round weather forecast. "Everyone has to play in those conditions and we'll just try our best to get the ball in the fairway and hit some greens."

There's still a lot at stake besides the trophy this week as players jockey for position in the tournament within the tournament.

The top 100 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings following the RSM Classic become exempt on the PGA Tour for the 2027 season. The FedEx Cup Fall also determines eligibility for early-season signature events, with Nos. 51-60 in the final standings earning spots in the 2027 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and 2027 Genesis Invitational.

Nos. 101-110 earn conditional status for the 2027 season via the 101-110 Prior Season FedEx Cup Fall Points List category, which is not subject to reshuffle

Nos. 111-125 earn conditional status for the 2027 season via the 111-125 Prior Season FedEx Cup Fall Points List category, which is subject to reshuffle

Nos. 126-150 earn conditional status for the 2027 season via the 126-150 Prior Season FedEx Cup Fall Points List category, which is subject to reshuffle. This category will earn limited access to PGA Tour events.

Three players are projected to move into the top 100. Neergaard-Peterson would leap from No. 106 to No. 57 and also gain two signature event starts with a win; Penge would vault from No. 120 to No. 65 should he claim the title; and Lee Hodges, who is one back and T-4, is protected to jump from No. 105 to No. 94.

Three players are projected to drop out of the top 100. John Parry and David Lipsky fell to Nos. 101 and 102 and both missed the cut and no longer control their own destiny. Christiaan Bezuidenhout rallied to make the cut and sits T-41. He entered the week as the 'Bubble Boy' at No. 100 and is currently projected at No. 103.
